question: A ski-lift maintenance shop tests a carrier on a short rail. The carrier's speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 0*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the drive-lever index. The carrier has a mass of 31000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 11 carriers on the rail. A charged latch then adds 15 J to that total, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The shop runs 2 identical rails. What total energy, in kJ, do the rails hold?

A demolition contractor has 8 anchor points on a test frame, and each shot braces a distinct set of 3 of them. The controller sets the test mass's speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to the number of distinct sets of 3 anchor points available. The test mass has a mass of 31000 g, and the site cabin is at 18 degrees C. The energy the mass carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 10 masses on a frame and then by the 6 frames on the site, and the site's total is expressed in kilojoules. The contractor works 9 identical sites. What total energy, in kJ, do the sites hold?

A brewery needs the total thrust, in newtons, from its crate-pusher line. Each pusher's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 13a + 42 = 0. The pusher carriage has a mass of 102 kg, the hall is kept at 12 degrees C, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A pre-load screw adds 1 N to that force, a guide pad then relieves 4 N, and a seal relieves a further 3 N. The line runs 11 identical pushers. What total thrust, in N, does the line deliver?

A cable-drum works needs the total figure, in kilojoules, held by its test hall. Two index wheels carry 141 teeth and 195 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. Each test slider then runs at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number; a slider has a mass of 45000 g, and the hall sits at 23 degrees C. The energy one slider carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 11 sliders on a bench, and the bench's figure is expressed in kilojoules. A rack holds 4 identical benches, and the hall holds 11 identical racks. What total figure, in kJ, does the hall hold?

A dockside conveyor is being rated. Two index wheels carry 43 teeth and 69 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The take-up carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number; the carriage has a mass of 153000 g, and the machinery house sits at 27 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the rating sheet expresses it in kilonewtons. The conveyor runs 4 identical drives. A belt tension of 22 kN and a scraper pre-load of 29 kN are then added to their combined figure. What figure, in kN, does the rating sheet show?

A pallet works needs the total energy, in joules, held by its transfer bank. Two index wheels carry 274 teeth and 314 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The first gearbox multiplies that number by 5, and a second gearbox multiplies the result by 4, giving the carriage's speed in metres per second. The carriage has a mass of 18 kg. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is the figure for a single carriage, and the bank holds 4 identical carriages. What total energy, in J, does the bank hold?

A model-railway laboratory runs a test wagon along a level track. The wagon's speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 6v + 8 = 0. The wagon has a mass of 6000 g, and the room is kept at 21 degrees C. The energy the wagon carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 10 wagons in the rake, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. A charged buffer adds 23 kJ to that figure, and a controller supply adds a further 13 kJ. What is the laboratory's total, in kJ?

A rope works needs the total figure, in kilojoules, for a haul-line trial. The test carriage's speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 12v + 35 = 0. The carriage has a mass of 22 kg, and the energy it carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 11 carriages on the line. The result is expressed in kilojoules, and a charged buffer then adds 11 kJ. The works runs 8 identical lines. What total figure, in kJ, does the works hold?

A pinball manufacturer is testing a plunger on the bench. The ball's launch speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 7v + 6 = 0. The ball has a mass of 10000 g, and the workshop is at 23 degrees C. To the energy the ball carries by virtue of its motion, 29 J is added for the spring latch. The bench fires 8 identical plungers, and the manufacturer runs 10 identical benches. What total energy, in J, do the benches hold?

An excavator maker is rating a boom cylinder. The boom's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 3*x^2 + 6*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the joystick index. The boom assembly has a mass of 95000 g, and the yard is at 19 degrees C. The cylinder supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a return spring adds 4 N to its load. A machine carries 6 identical cylinders, and a hose pre-load of 9 N is then added to the machine's combined load. What total load, in kN, does the machine carry?

A lift company needs the final figure, in kilonewtons, for a car-frame test. The frame builds its rate of change of speed in 2 identical steps, and each step contributes 3 m/s^2 while the brake releases and a further 9 m/s^2 while the motor drives. The frame has a mass of 132 kg, and the machine room is at 24 degrees C. The motor supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a guide shoe relieves 16 N of it. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons, a counterweight then adds 14 kN, and a compensating rope adds a further 29 kN. What is the final figure, in kN?

A sledging club is instrumenting a straight run. The sled's speed v, in m/s, is the larger value that satisfies v^2 - 7v + 6 = 0. The sled has a mass of 30 kg, and the snow is at 2 degrees C. The energy the sled carries by virtue of its motion is multiplied by the 8 sleds on the run, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The club runs 2 identical shifts and holds 7 identical meetings in the season. What total energy, in kJ, does the season account for?

A conveyor maker needs the total figure, in kilojoules, held by a whole warehouse. Each tote's speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 9v + 8 = 0. A tote has a mass of 27 kg, and the warehouse is kept at 18 degrees C. The energy one tote carries by virtue of its motion is expressed in kilojoules. A lane holds 4 identical totes, an aisle holds 4 lanes, and the warehouse holds 6 identical aisles. What total figure, in kJ, does the warehouse hold?

A conveyor plant is setting up a new head drive. Two change gears carry 240 teeth and 345 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The head carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number, and the carriage has a mass of 48000 g. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the rating sheet expresses it in kilonewtons. The plant runs 8 identical drives; a scraper then relieves 1 kN of their combined figure, and a take-up jack adds 5 kN. What figure, in kN, does the rating sheet show?

A wire-drawing shop measures a capstan block on a short run. The block's position along its guide is, in metres, 5*t^3 - 5*t^2 with t in seconds, and the shop is held at 25 degrees C. The measurement is taken at the instant t = 1 s, when the block has a mass of 41000 g and moves at whatever speed its position curve then gives. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and the shop runs 7 identical blocks. A charged buffer then adds 23 kJ to their combined figure. What is the shop's total, in kJ?

A forging plant needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a hammer trial. The hammer's position along its guide is, in metres, 5*t^3 + 4*t^2 with t in seconds, and the trial is scored at the instant t = 2 s by differentiating that position 2 times. The value obtained is set as the test slug's speed in metres per second; the slug has a mass of 39000 g, and the shop sits at 29 degrees C. The energy the slug carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 2 hammers that strike together, and a latch then adds 26 J. The result is expressed in kilojoules, and a standing instrument allowance of 8 kJ is subtracted. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A toy factory needs the final figure, in joules, for a launcher test. Two index wheels carry 49 teeth and 237 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The dart is then launched at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number; it has a mass of 6000 g, and the test room is at 22 degrees C. To the energy the dart carries by virtue of that motion, 27 J is added for the spring, and 25 J is then deducted for the barrel friction. The factory tests 3 identical launchers. What is the final figure, in J?

A rolling mill needs the final entry, in kilojoules, for a coiler trial. The coiler arm's position along its guide is, in metres, 5*t^3 + 0*t^2 with t in seconds, and the trial is scored at the instant t = 1 s by differentiating that position 2 times. The value obtained is set as the test strip's speed in metres per second; the strip has a mass of 10 kg, and the mill floor is at 30 degrees C. To the energy the strip carries by virtue of that motion, 8 J is added for the gripper. The mill runs 7 identical coilers and expresses their combined figure in kilojoules, and a charged buffer then adds 13 kJ. What is the final entry, in kJ?

A sugar refinery is rating a centrifuge drive. Two index wheels carry 339 teeth and 211 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly. The basket carriage's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is set numerically equal to that number; the carriage has a mass of 193 kg, and the process floor is at 32 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and a pre-load screw adds 3 N to its load. The result is expressed in kilonewtons; a station holds 11 identical drives, and the refinery has 8 identical stations. What total figure, in kN, does the refinery show?

A tunnel-boring contractor needs the net figure, in kilonewtons, for a cutterhead drive. The cutterhead's rate of change of speed, in m/s^2, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 5*x between x = 2 and x = 3, where x is the thrust-lever index. The cutterhead has a mass of 170 kg, and the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, expressed in kilonewtons. A shield friction allowance of 21 kN is subtracted from that figure, a grip-pad allowance of 30 kN is subtracted next, and a seal allowance of 13 kN is subtracted last. What is the net figure, in kN?

A bungee-testing laboratory drops a mass down a guided tower. The mass's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 2*x^2 + 3*x between x = 2 and x = 4, where x is the release-cam index. The dropped mass is 56000 g, and the tower is at 15 degrees C. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is multiplied by the 2 masses released together, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. The laboratory runs 2 identical towers and completes 7 identical programmes. What total energy, in kJ, do the programmes account for?

A pile-testing contractor needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a drop-weight campaign. The weight's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 3*x^2 + 8*x between x = 1 and x = 3, where x is the winch-index setting. The weight has a mass of 45000 g, and the site cabin is at 13 degrees C. The energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules, and the campaign covers 12 identical drops. A rig allowance of 26 kJ is subtracted from the campaign total, and an instrument allowance of 21 kJ is subtracted as well. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A launch-rail manufacturer needs the total thrust, in kilonewtons, from a complete installation. The raw index is the area under the curve 3*x^2 + 0*x between x = 0 and x = 3, where x is the throttle index, and a control offset then adds 14 to that index, giving the carriage's rate of change of speed in m/s^2. The carriage has a mass of 81000 g, and each drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. A rail carries 8 identical drives, and their combined force is expressed in kilonewtons. The installation has 7 identical rails. What total thrust, in kN, does the installation deliver?

An archery club needs the final figure, in kilojoules, at the foot of its bow-test sheet. The base speed b, in m/s, is the smaller value satisfying b^2 - 15*b + 56 = 0, and the limbs send the arrow away at 3 times that base speed. The arrow has a mass of 3 kg, and the range is at 17 degrees C. The energy the arrow carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A standing instrument allowance of 14 kJ is then added to it. What is the final figure, in kJ?

A laboratory needs the total energy, in joules, from a paired launcher test. The trolley's release speed, in metres per second, is the area under the curve 1*x^2 + 1*x between x = 1 and x = 4, where x is the cam setting. The trolley has a mass of 6 kg. To the energy it carries by virtue of that motion, 14 J is added for the latch and a further 15 J for the trigger coil. The laboratory runs 2 identical launchers. What is the total, in J?
